subject: Agriculture
title: Biofortification
description: A quick, practical guide to Biofortification.

hook.text: Two billion people suffer from hidden hunger—not calorie shortage, but micronutrient deficiency.

buildup.text: Staple crops like rice and wheat are calorie-rich but nutrient-poor. They fill stomachs but starve bodies.

discovery.text: Biofortification breeds extra iron, zinc, or vitamins directly into food crops—no supplements needed.

twist.text: Orange-fleshed sweet potatoes with high vitamin A are already saving children's eyesight in Mozambique and Uganda.

climax.text: HarvestPlus has released biofortified varieties of 12 crops in 30 countries. Nutrition is bred, not added.

punchline.text: Better nutrition, same seed. The crop does the supplementing.

quiz.question: What is biofortification?
options: Breeding extra micronutrients directly into crop varieties

details.summary: Biofortification breeds essential micronutrients directly into staple crops to address hidden hunger—the micronutrient deficiencies that affect over 2 billion people who get enough calories but lack essential vitamins and minerals.
details.whyItMatters: Hidden hunger causes stunted growth, cognitive impairment, and premature death in billions of people who eat adequate calories but lack iron, zinc, and vitamin A. Biofortification delivers nutrients through the foods people already eat.
takeaways: Hidden hunger from micronutrient deficiency affects over 2 billion people globally
Iron-biofortified beans now reach millions of farmers in Rwanda, DR Congo, and Uganda
Orange-fleshed sweet potato provides vitamin A to millions of children in sub-Saharan Africa

faq.question: How does biofortification work compared to food supplementation?
faq.answer: Biofortification breeds higher nutrient levels directly into crop varieties using conventional breeding or biotechnology. Once a biofortified variety is developed, it costs nothing extra for farmers to grow.

faq.question: Which biofortified crops have been most successful?
faq.answer: Orange-fleshed sweet potato (vitamin A) has reached over 10 million African households. Iron beans are grown by millions in Central and East Africa. Zinc wheat is released in Pakistan and India. Iron pearl millet is grown in India. HarvestPlus coordinates biofortification research globally.
